candidates.title: Released Dave clocks (COMMITMENT_BUDGET 120 min, log2step [38,0]) are sized for average uarch density; a guest's TLB-flush-dense region makes one level-1 commitment cost ~30x that (about 18 h on the audit host), so the honest claim cannot join within its clock (A7)
candidates.component: Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 released arbitration constants and clocks (prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol, CanonicalTournamentParametersProvider.sol, ClockBudgets.sol), together with the emulator's per-mcycle uarch cost (uarch program, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes)
candidates.role: Referee model (the deployed referee, AUDIT.md component table); the per-mcycle cost comes from components in the honest-operator role (uarch program, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes)
candidates.location: bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/arbitration-config/ArbitrationConstants.sol (LEVELS=2, log2step=[38,0], height=[54,38], COMMITMENT_BUDGET=120 minutes); ClockBudgets.sol refill()/maxAllowance(); Tournament.sol:786 (child-return refill commitmentBudget+2*responseBudget); the sizing rationale is in bugs/harness/work/dave/released/docs/dimensioning.md 'The rule' ('Clocks are dimensioned to the average case') and docs/measurements/constants.md (density label 566 usteps per big cycle). Emulator side: src/interpret.cpp set_prv() line 380 and the sfence.vma/satp/MPRV paths (flush_all_tlb, flush_tlb_set), src/machine.cpp collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes() line 2757.
candidates.description: With the released constants, an inner (level-1) tournament's leaf commitment covers 2^38 meta-cycles = 2^18 mcycles x 2^20 uarch cycles, and building it requires executing every one of those 2^18 mcycles in the uarch and hashing the state after each uarch cycle. COMMITMENT_BUDGET (120 min, refilled per child) was derived from the stress workload's AVERAGE density of 566 executed usteps per mcycle with a hardware slack of 2 and a further doubling (constants.md, dimensioning.md: 'clocks are sized to average density plus a hardware slack factor - not to the worst instruction repeated wall to wall'). The threat model instead requires A7 to cover 'the worst-case costs of R12'. The per-mcycle uarch cost is guest-chosen: every sfence.vma, satp ASID/MODE write, and every privilege change (each trap and each xRET that changes privilege, via set_prv) flushes all 3x256 TLB slots, and the uarch performs each slot as a separate write_tlb ecall (about 22.8 usteps per slot). Measured on this branch: wall-to-wall sfence.vma = 17,322 usteps per mcycle (31.8x the 544 of an addi loop, 30.6x Dave's 566 label); building the uarch hashes with collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes costs 245 ms per mcycle against 8.6 ms for addi (28.5x). A 2^18-mcycle leaf of such code takes 17.9 h on the audit host; scaling Dave's own measured cold join (1542 s for a 2^18-mcycle stress leaf, node-vs-emulator.md) by 28.5x gives about 12 h. Both exceed the 120-minute budget by 6x to 9x. The excess draws on the non-rechargeable censorship allowance C, which every forced inner tournament drains again. A U-mode ecall loop with a one-instruction M-mode handler already reaches 6,425 usteps per mcycle (11.8x). FP square root and division reach about 4x. A normal Linux shell app (the harness echo template) measures 576.
candidates.trigger: An input sender whose input makes the guest (after taking control of the kernel or firmware, which section 4 allows, or a bare-metal or kernel-level application by design) run a region dense in sfence.vma, satp writes or privilege changes, inside the input's bounded mcycle budget. A dispute adversary then steers a level-0 match to a leaf (gap) inside that region. That forces the honest claim to build and join a level-1 commitment over 2^18 dense mcycles, and to do so again in each of the logarithmically many matches it is forced into.
candidates.reachability: Reachable. Any assignment of guest-writable memory and registers is presumed reachable (section 2), and the guest may run any instruction stream at any privilege level (section 4). sfence.vma in S/M mode, satp writes and traps are ordinary instructions. The application still follows the rollup interface and bounds its mcycle usage, because the density lives inside the bounded mcycles of a normally accepted input. A correctly designed application is constrained only in its mcycle count (section 2, 'Correctly designed application'), not in its uarch cycles per mcycle.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The trigger is not on the list. It needs a deployment that violates A7, but section 8 keeps that in scope 'unless the emulator's own behavior is what makes the obligation fail, such as a worst-case cost or proof size larger than the deployment was sized for, or unless an implementation of the referee model is what violates it (section 3)'. Both exceptions apply: the released Dave referee is the referee model (AUDIT.md), and the worst-case cost is the emulator's per-mcycle uarch cost. It is not 'Average-case performance', because the worst case is what changes. 2 Role: Dave released = Referee model (AUDIT.md). Section 3: 'A defect that only changes how long a claim may take to respond, or only crashes or stalls the model ... is rated as support.' The cost itself is shown by components in the honest-operator role (uarch program, collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes). 3 High/Medium cases: if the defect is read as a clock-sizing defect of the referee model, it only changes how long a claim may take to respond, so it is rated as support. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. That gives Medium. 4 Critical: otherwise, the defect is the case 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make unbounded, super-linear, or larger than what the deployment was sized for' (the operation is a uarch-level claim). It also violates A7: 'The dispute constants and clocks leave room for the honest claim to play the logarithmic number of matches that a tournament forces on it, at the worst-case costs of R12 ... No rule of the referee may make the honest claim lose by timeout while it acts within its own clock.' Breaking A7 in turn breaks R4: 'The honest operator observes the chain and submits its transactions within the dispute clocks.' That gives Critical. 5 Not needed. Deciding facts: (a) whether a clock sized below the worst-case R12 cost counts as 'only changes how long a claim may take to respond' (Medium) or as a deployment A7 failure caused by the emulator's worst-case cost (Critical); (b) the deployment's censorship allowance C and the number of forced inner tournaments, which set how many dense joins the honest claim survives (on Ethereum C is a week, so about 10 forced joins at 16 h overrun each; on the testnet deployments C is hours, so one join).
candidates.claimed_severity: Critical (reading: worst-case R12 cost larger than the deployment was sized for, A7). Medium if read as a referee-model clock defect rated as support.
candidates.threat_to_goal: Completeness failure: 'The honest operator ... cannot respond in time. If the honest claim is eliminated, a dishonest claim can win.' The level-1 join does not fit COMMITMENT_BUDGET at the worst-case density, so a Sybil adversary that forces enough dense inner tournaments exhausts the honest claim's allowance. The honest claim loses by timeout, and a fabricated final state, with its outputs, can settle.
candidates.evidence: Bare-metal guests built with bugs/harness/baremetal/build.sh (sources in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R12/g/: loop.S variants v0..v8 and sf.S) and measured with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R12/measure.lua, sf.lua, native.lua and linux-density.lua. Results: addi 544 usteps/mcycle, 8.6-10 ms/mcycle uarch collect; wall-to-wall sfence.vma 17,322 usteps/mcycle, 245 ms/mcycle (2^18 mcycles = 17.9 h); csrw satp alternation 7,222 avg (one flush per instruction, about 17.6k each); U-ecall + 1-instruction M handler 6,425 avg; fdiv.d 2,276; fsqrt.d 2,133 (alternating with j); div 678; mulhu 780; fmadd.d 835. Valid-template Linux echo app processing one input: 56M mcycles, sampled 576 usteps/mcycle. Dave's own documents admit the gap: dimensioning.md lines 20-32 call such 'un-disputable' machines (the 'sqrt / TLB-flush class') excluded by a trusted-app assumption, which the threat model does not grant.
candidates.test_idea: Deterministic test with no wall clock: build the sf.S guest (64 x sfence.vma; j), run 1000 mcycles, then for N=64 mcycles run_uarch(2^20), read uarch_cycle and reset_uarch. Compute the projected level-1 commitment cost as (usteps per mcycle / 566) x (the 60-minute derivation's leaf time), or simply require that the worst-case usteps per mcycle times 2^18 times Dave's measured per-ustep collect rate (from constants.md: 173 big cycles/s at 566 usteps, i.e. 97,918 usteps/s) fits COMMITMENT_BUDGET read from the released ArbitrationConstants (7200 s). The test exits 1 when 17,322 x 2^18 / 97,918 s = 46,371 s > 7,200 s, and 0 if either the constants are sized for the worst case or the worst-case density drops below the budget.

candidates.title: Every TLB flush rewrites all 768 slots, including ones already invalid, through a non-inlined 14-instruction ecall wrapper: one sfence.vma, satp write or privilege change costs ~17.3k uarch cycles (~22.8 per slot, ~4 would suffice) and ~640 ns natively (250x an addi), multiplying the worst-case mcycle and uarch-level-claim cost
candidates.component: Interpreter TLB flush (src/interpret.cpp) as compiled into the uarch program (uarch/uarch-bridge-state-access.hpp, uarch/uarch-ecall.c), and the native interpreter
candidates.role: Honest operator (interpreter, uarch program); every honest mcycle and uarch-level claim pays this cost
candidates.location: src/interpret.cpp: set_prv() 380-391 (flush_all_tlb on every privilege change); flush_tlb_slot()/flush_tlb_set()/flush_all_tlb()/flush_tlb_vaddr() 892-937 (unconditional write of every slot, even an already-invalid one); sfence.vma 3585-3610 (flush_tlb_vaddr flushes all three sets); satp write ~2276; MPRV paths ~497, ~2855. uarch/uarch-ecall.c:44-59 ua_write_tlb_ECALL, compiled to 14 instructions (uarch/uarch-ram.elf.objdump 0x600b90-0x600bc4: 12 redundant register moves plus the ecall and the return) and called from an 8-instruction loop body (0x602430-0x60244c), so each slot costs about 22.8 uarch cycles.
candidates.description: A full TLB flush is 768 calls to write_tlb, one per slot, whether or not the slot already holds TLB_INVALID_PAGE. In the uarch each call is a function call to a wrapper that copies a0-a4 into temporaries and back before the ecall, so a flush costs about 17,300 uarch cycles. Each of those cycles costs the honest operator one hash-tree update and one leaf (about 14-18 us each in collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes). The same flush in a loop that keeps the constant arguments in place and issues the ecall inline costs about 4 uarch cycles per slot (about 3.1k per flush). Skipping slots that are already invalid would cost about 3-4 uarch cycles per slot (load, compare, branch), and those cycles dirty no words. Natively the same 768 writes plus dirty tracking make one sfence.vma cost about 640 ns per mcycle under run, and about 2.6 us under collect_mcycle_root_hashes, against 2.5 ns and 22 ns for an addi. Because set_prv flushes on every privilege change, every trap and every xRET pays the flush. A guest that alternates TLB-flushing instructions sets the worst-case cost of 'an mcycle' and of 'a uarch-level claim' (both R12 operations) at about 5x what the same flush would cost without this overhead, and at about 30x the cost of an ordinary instruction.
candidates.trigger: Guest code (after an input; any privilege level) executing sfence.vma, satp ASID/MODE writes, or repeated traps and returns. Each such instruction is one mcycle.
candidates.reachability: Reachable from any valid template whose guest runs privileged code, which section 4 assumes an input can obtain. Even U-mode code pays two full flushes per ecall or fault.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? No. It is triggered by guest instructions at reachable states. It is not 'Average-case performance', because it sets the worst case of an mcycle and of a uarch-level claim. 2 Role: interpreter and uarch program = Honest operator (AUDIT.md table). 3 High: 'A defect that lets the guest, or host load that the deployment was sized for, multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor, compared with the same operation without the defect ... A cost that the specified semantics require is not a defect. When the sizing is unknown, rate such a constant-factor increase High.' The specified semantics require only that the TLB be invalid after the flush. Rewriting already-invalid slots, and doing so through a wrapper that wastes about 18 of every 22.8 uarch cycles, is not required by those semantics (writes of identical values leave the hashed state unchanged). That gives High. If triage holds that the deployed sizing (candidate 1) does not cover even the reduced cost, the Critical entry 'An operation listed in R12 whose worst-case cost a guest can make ... larger than what the deployment was sized for' applies to the joint effect. 4/5 Not reached. Note: fixing it changes the uarch program and the access sequence of a logged transition, so it creates a new protocol version (R13).
candidates.threat_to_goal: It removes the margin A7 relies on: it multiplies by about 5x the worst-case honest cost of every uarch-level claim the tournament can force, and by about 250x the worst-case native mcycle relative to ordinary code, the cost that the root (level-0) build and positioning pay. Combined with average-case clock sizing (candidate 1), this is what pushes a forced join from a few hours to more than ten.
candidates.evidence: Measured uarch cycles per mcycle (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R12/sf.lua, measure.lua): sfence.vma 17,322 (768 slots, about 22.6 each); satp alternation about 17.6k per write; addi 544. Native (native.lua): sfence half-loop 349 ns/mcycle under run (so about 640-700 ns per sfence), 1,295 ns/mcycle under collect_mcycle_root_hashes, against addi at 2.5 and 22.2 ns. Disassembly: uarch/uarch-ram.elf.objdump at 0x600b90 (wrapper) and 0x602418-0x6024b0 (flush_all_tlb with three 256-iteration loops).
candidates.test_idea: Load sf.S (64 x sfence.vma; j), run 1000 mcycles, run_uarch(2^20) over one sfence mcycle and assert uarch_cycle <= 768*6 + 600 (an inlined ecall loop, or a skip of invalid slots). It fails at about 17,300. A second assertion: the uarch cycles of an sfence.vma executed when every slot is already invalid do not exceed those of a few dozen loads.

candidates.title: PRT bridge fetches the shared tournament factory's logs unfiltered and, like the epoch listener, re-sorts and rescans all accumulated logs on every observation: honest work grows with foreign chain activity (permissionless instantiate spam) and quadratically with inputs and matches
candidates.component: PRT bridge and epoch listener in doc/recipes (prt-bridge.lua observe(), prt-epoch.lua poll(), prt-log-history.lua)
candidates.role: Support (AUDIT.md: 'No production deployment runs the player, the bridge or the CLI'), standing in for the honest operator
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt-bridge.lua:47-200 observe() (addresses {factory, consensus, root} fetched with no topics; every observation copies every log ever fetched since the seal into a new table, sorts it with table.sort, and replays all of them into contexts/matches/events). doc/recipes/prt-epoch.lua:25-66 poll() (copies and sorts all logs of the epoch and rebuilds positions/blocks on every poll). doc/recipes/prt-log-history.lua keeps every log forever (self.logs). Dave MultiLevelTournamentFactory.instantiate() is external and permissionless and emits TournamentCreated (bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/tournament/factories/MultiLevelTournamentFactory.sol:79-92; ITournamentFactory.sol:16 says 'Anyone can call instantiate').
candidates.description: The bridge needs only its own root's TournamentCreated, yet it fetches every log the factory emits after the seal. The factory is shared by every application and anyone can call instantiate, so foreign or spam root tournaments land in the honest bridge's history and are re-sorted and re-scanned on every observation. More generally, observe() and poll() cost O(n log n) in the number of logs accumulated since the seal (or since the previous epoch's seal for inputs), per observation. That is not a bounded cost per input or per match. The total over an epoch's life is quadratic: each poll rescans up to 2^24 InputAdded logs, and each tick rescans all logs of every match and Sybil commitment.
candidates.trigger: An adversary calls factory.instantiate repeatedly (each is a cheap clone) while an honest epoch's dispute is open, or sends many inputs, or posts many Sybil claims and moves. The honest bridge observes at every tick.
candidates.reachability: Reachable on any chain where the factory is shared or callable by anyone, which Dave's factory is. Inputs and Sybils are adversary capabilities (section 7).
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Out of scope? The bridge is not a validator node, nor a dishonest strategy or a test harness, so it is in scope as support. 2 Role: Support (AUDIT.md). Section 3: 'implementations of an operator that no deployment runs ... A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for'. 3/4 In the honest-operator role this violates R12: 'The honest operator's own work outside the emulator, such as observing the chain ... has a bounded cost per input, per yield, and per match, and its total grows only with the inputs, yields, and matches of the epochs still open. That total must not grow ... with chain activity that does not belong to the application.' It is reachable on the honest operator's path, so it would be Critical (step 4), and as support it is Medium. 5 n/a.
candidates.threat_to_goal: In an operator implementation, factory spam or input and Sybil floods could slow observation enough to miss clocks (a completeness failure). Here it is shown only by the support player.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. Factory logs are requested without topics (prt-bridge.lua:68, get_logs_of(addresses, first_blocks)); in contrast prt-epoch.lua filters the InputBox by app topic, which shows the intent. The full rescan and sort happen on each observe() and poll() call.
candidates.test_idea: Against a mock chain (prt-bridge-test.lua style), seal an epoch, then emit K TournamentCreated logs from the factory for other tournaments, and count the logs the bridge decodes or keeps in history over T observations. Assert that the count is independent of K and that the per-observation work does not grow with already-processed logs (for example, wrap the chain's logs() and the abi decoder with counters).

candidates.title: collect_uarch_cycle_bundle (and collect_mcycle_bundle) materialize every repeated fixed-point leaf: one 2^20 bundle costs ~1.3 s and ~300 MB for an mcycle of ~550 uarch cycles, not a bounded amount per run of repetitions
candidates.component: Machine API collect_uarch_cycle_bundle / collect_mcycle_bundle (C, Lua, JSON-RPC)
candidates.role: Rest of the machine API: honest operator if a production node calls it to open bundles, otherwise support
candidates.location: src/machine.cpp:2989-3033 collect_uarch_cycle_bundle (hashes.reserve(2^log2) and hashes.insert(halt_count, halt_root_hash)); src/machine.cpp:2597-2673 collect_mcycle_bundle (hashes.reserve(bundle_mcycle_count) before running; hashes.resize(bundle_mcycle_count, fixed_point_root_hash))
candidates.description: R12 asks that repetitions of a fixed point cost a bounded amount per run. These bundle APIs return the full expanded list of 2^log2 hashes, padding with copies of the uarch-halted or fixed-point hash, and pass it through JSON base64 for the C, Lua and JSON-RPC bindings. For log2=20 (one mcycle's whole uarch span, the natural bundle for a node that bundles per big cycle), one call allocates 32 MiB of hashes plus about 45 MB of JSON and a 2^20-entry Lua table, independent of the about 550 uarch cycles actually executed.
candidates.trigger: The honest operator (its node) opening a uarch bundle with a large log2_bundle_uarch_cycle_count, or an mcycle bundle that a halted guest pads.
candidates.reachability: Reachable for any state. Every mcycle has a halted uarch tail.
candidates.rating_steps: 1 Not excluded. 2 Role: rest of the machine API. Honest operator where a production node calls it (Dave's node uses cm_collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes, as node-vs-emulator.md shows), otherwise support. 3 High case 'multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor' (about 16x in time and about 300 MB per call for log2=20), unless triage holds that returning the expanded list is 'a cost that the specified semantics require', in which case it is Low. As support, Medium at most. 4/5 n/a.
candidates.claimed_severity: High if a production node opens bundles through this API with large bundles; Low otherwise
candidates.threat_to_goal: Constant-factor amplification of proof-time cost and memory, removing A7 margin. No wrong hash.
candidates.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r1/R12/bundle.lua: collect_uarch_cycle_root_hashes(1 mcycle, bundle 0) returned 557 hashes in 81.7 ms; collect_uarch_cycle_bundle(0, 20) returned 1,048,576 hashes in 1,290 ms; peak RSS 343 MB.
candidates.test_idea: Assert that collect_uarch_cycle_bundle(0, 20) on an addi guest allocates at most a bounded multiple of the executed uarch cycles (for example, check the peak RSS delta < 16 MB, or that the returned representation run-length encodes the halt tail).

not_covered: store/load/clone/sync cost (linearity in bytes, sparse files, dht/dpt rebuild on O1 adoption) was not measured

hash-tree update cost per dirty page / page-hash cache worst case (e.g. guest dirtying one word in many pages per period), get_proof cost, and update_words per uarch cycle beyond the instructions tested

worst-case uarch cycles of instructions not tested: Sv57 page walks with TLB misses, misaligned/page-crossing accesses, AMOs, interrupts combined with traps, CSR paths other than satp; only the instruction classes listed in the evidence were measured
delivery (send_cmio_response) and reset log sizes and their on-chain gas/transaction-size fit (R12 per-transaction limits) were not measured; EVM harness not used
console output cost per mcycle (flush modes) and soft-yield paths
PRT player per-match/per-yield storage growth (stored machine cache, per-epoch directories, outputs) and restart cost were not inspected beyond prt-log-history/bridge/epoch observation loops
Lua frontier-forest fixed-point padding costs (cartesi.hash-tree frontier_forest_pad_back/expand_leaf) and fixed-point-tree memory were not verified against 'bounded per run'
level-0 (root) commitment sizing vs worst-case native mcycle cost (about 250x for TLB flushes) was not quantified against Dave's root slowdown budget
JSON-RPC server/client paths for large collect results (memory of base64 JSON) beyond the one Lua measurement
